items.title: A $131 Billion Shot in the Arm: How Boeing’s New F-15 Deal Can Help Shares
items.summary: Boeing  just secured a $131 billion contract for its F-15 fighter jet.  It’s significant for Boeing’s struggling defense division, which generated first-half 2026 sales of $15.1 billion.  “That’s a lot of F-15 support,” wrote Vertical Research Partners analyst Rob Stallard on Tuesday, noting that the contract covers maintenance and upgrades.

items.title: Boeing (BA) Lands $131 Billion F 15 Defense Contract
items.summary: Boeing (NYSE:BA) has secured a new US$131b contract for its F-15 fighter jet program, covering production, maintenance and upgrades. The multi year defense agreement is set to support Boeing's defense segment after several years of operational and reputational challenges. The contract is expected to add materially to Boeing's backlog and long term revenue visibility for its F-15 line. items.title: Boeing’s New F-15 Contract Could Bolster Its Defense Business
items.summary: Boeing clinched a multiyear contract worth up to $131 billion to serve the U.S. Air Force's F-15 program, offering the plane maker a rich opportunity to grow its defense business over the next decade.  The contract announced yesterday covers potential payments for upgrades, retrofits and maintenance work across F-15 fleets in the U.S. and with foreign buyers including Japan, Israel and Saudi Arabia.  The exact quantity of jets on order and the delivery schedule still need to be worked out.
